subject: Food Science
title: Microbial Contamination Sources
description: A short lesson to help you apply Microbial Contamination Sources.

hook.text: A single sneeze launches 40,000 droplets at 160 km/h. Each droplet can carry thousands of bacteria.

buildup.text: Microbes reach food through soil, water, air, animals, human handlers, and equipment—contamination is everywhere.

discovery.text: Cross-contamination—raw chicken juices touching salad—causes more foodborne illness than undercooked food itself.

twist.text: Your kitchen sponge harbors more bacteria per square inch than your toilet seat. It's the dirtiest item in the house.

climax.text: Proper hand washing for 20 seconds reduces bacterial transfer by 99%. Most people wash for only 6 seconds.

punchline.text: Contamination is inevitable. The question is whether you control it.

quiz.question: What causes more foodborne illness than undercooked food?
options: Cross-contamination between raw and ready-to-eat foods
